Critic web3_clientVersion queries on 2026-11-27 found the builds that cycle 29 recorded: ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com reth/v2.11.0-b9abbcc (block 0x1946d26), mainnet.optimism.io op-reth/v0.0.0-dev-unknown, mainnet.base.org reth/v2.5.2-9e380dd/base/v1.5.6, mainnet.unichain.org, rpc-gel.inkonchain.com and rpc.soneium.org op-reth/v2.10.0-rc.4-65e80332, rpc.zora.energy conduit-op-reth/v2.5.1-8f0ccac, worldchain-mainnet.g.alchemy.com world-chain/v2.8.2-9596311, mainnet.megaeth.com mega-reth/v2.3.1-4499c42, rpc.mainnet.arc.io 'arc/v1'. Nothing is known to have regressed. Arc's endpoint string names no release, so no cycle 30 result can be tied to a build there.

Second cycle in a row with no unit holding L5 or L6. BNB Chain Jenner (2026-12-08 02:30 UTC), Polygon Salvador (block 98,688,600, about 14:00 UTC the same day) and Tempo T14 (15:00 UTC the same day, T15 on 15 December) fall before or during cycle 31. The day-one high leads L-545, L-1032, L-1075 and L-1076 are still open. established-l1 rehearsed Salvador under a block number override (L-1191, 185,529 vectors), which closes the cycle 29 gap on the rehearsal, but L-1191 is inconclusive because the override cannot run the BlockAlloc code write that is Salvador's only effect, and no tagged bor release carries Salvador.

theme-monad-gcc-allocator-model ran the gcc 15.2.0 register allocator, spill path and write_to_final_stack_offsets on random Stack states (seeds 3030 to 3034), not on the states the PoolManager's compiled blocks produce. theme-monad-mined-native-coverage shows 128 value-computing compiled blocks that no mined transaction entered since v0.16.7 reached mainnet on 2026-11-26, 56 of them with emitted code changed at v0.16.7, including FullMath.mulDiv 512-bit path copies. Any account can enter those blocks with one transaction, and consensus on Monad checks validators against each other, all of which run the same gcc build. L-1172 was cleared on the clang harness and its text says the gcc build was not executed.

Elysium answers nitro/vlocal+unknown-unknown on go1.25.12, a build that names no source. theme-nitro-binary-arith-lift lifted only the b72783f binaries of Arbitrum One and Robinhood Chain. Elysium rests on RPC vectors and mined swaps alone, and it is the only network on its toolchain.

arbitrum-family cleared core/vm on OffchainLabs/go-ethereum master, while theme-nitro-binary-arith-lift showed that the shipped b72783f binary lacks execUntraced, execTraced and layeredJumpDests of v1.17.10 and still uses makeDup and makePush closures, so master is not the source of the shipped build. The source clearance holds for arithmetic only because the binary lift covers the same handlers. SLOAD, SSTORE, TLOAD, TSTORE, the call family, RETURNDATACOPY, the isCode map path and the ArbOS tx hooks have been read only at master or the public fork, never in the binary. The lift's coverage table also leaves udivrem 36 of 204, udivremBy1 16 of 72, Div 17 of 80, Mod 11 of 84, SRsh 19 of 114 and Exp 17 of 166 instructions unreached. The unit says these are stack growth and panic paths but does not list their addresses.

theme-tempo-binary-storage-journal lifted TSTORE, TLOAD, the transient arms of rollback and the SSTORE writers from both v1.19.1 binaries. The AccountChange arm of rollback (native value and nonce undo), the account and slot hashbrown lookups, the CALL family with execute_call_message checkpoints, LOG, precompile dispatch and the TIP-1060 accounting inside SSTORE are still unlifted. The release that carries T15 (15 December) is not yet published at download.tempo.xyz/binaries/.

Replay windows are stuck on backends that lack history: Avalanche has 5,034 of 20,000 transactions untraced (14,966 done), and BNB Chain stays at 14,274 because bsc.api.pocket.network answers 'required historical state unavailable (reexec=128)'. Neither unit tried a backend other than pocket for the old blocks.

No PoolManager Swap or ModifyLiquidity log after block 52,134,672, so the follow-mode comparison of the closed validator's writes against replicas (L-1061) could not run. The 552-slot comparison over the 50 newest blocks is retrospective and reads replicas that replay what the producer already wrote.

leads.question: Rebuild the cycle 28 clang harness (cycles/027/theme-monad-engine-agreement.work/scripts/build.sh) with a dump of the virtual stack (element locations, free register queues, available stack offsets) at entry to each compiled PoolManager block, then run the gcc 15.2.0 model of cycle 30 (theme-monad-gcc-allocator-model.work/scripts allocdrv.py, shiftfull.py, wfso.py) from those exact states over the 128 value-computing blocks that no mined transaction entered since v0.16.7, starting with the FullMath.mulDiv 512-bit copies at 0x5757, 0x57ca, 0x5860, 0x588a, 0x58d6 and 0x58db. Does any block exit write a word other than the clang harness and pyevm.py write?
leads.why: These blocks are reachable by any account with one swap or position change, and Monad validators all run the same gcc binary. A wrong mulDiv or price word there would be certified by consensus while every RPC result, which comes from the interpreter, looks correct. That could become an unprivileged critical finding. Merges the two medium Monad leads of cycle 30.

leads.question: Once the code of the five Salvador BlockAlloc targets is known (from a tagged bor release or eth_getCode after block 98,688,600), what does each return when the PoolManager address is the caller of an empty value call (P1), transfer(address,uint256) (P2) and a balanceOf(PoolManager) staticcall (P3), run with eth_call from the PoolManager and a code override at block 98,688,599?
leads.why: L-751 found no target the PoolManager or its currencies use, but nobody has run the five new codes against the three call shapes an ordinary caller can make the PoolManager send. A target that reports or moves the native balance would be a new face of POL next to 0x1010 (F-008, F-100).

leads.question: List the addresses of the uint256 instructions the cycle 30 lift left unreached in the b72783f binaries (udivrem 36, udivremBy1 16, Div 17, Mod 11, SMod 9, SDiv 11, SRsh 19, Exp 17, AddMod 7, MulMod 7, reduce4 15, Reciprocal 16). Is each one a stack growth, morestack or panic path? If not, what operand shape reaches it, and does that shape occur in FullMath.mulDiv (src/libraries/FullMath.sol:24-48) or SqrtPriceMath?
leads.why: The lift reports 0 mismatches, but its coverage table leaves branches of the division and reduction routines unrun. The claim that all of them are runtime paths is not itemised. A reachable unreached branch is the one place a fault in the shipped arm64 or amd64 build could still hide.

leads.question: In the b72783f binaries, do opSload, opSstore, opTload, opTstore and the StateDB transient map methods they call, together with the journal revert of transient entries, give the stock result in the cycle 30 x86-64 and AArch64 models for the PoolManager's delta, count, lock and reserve slots, including after a reverted inner frame?
leads.why: Transient storage is the whole settlement ledger (src/libraries/CurrencyDelta.sol:21-39, NonzeroDeltaCount.sol:14-32, Lock.sol:13-25). The Nitro reading of it is at master, which the binary lift showed is not the shipped source. A delta that survives a revert in the shipped build would let a caller keep a credit it did not pay.

leads.question: Does Kinetiq publish a container image or binary for the nitro/vlocal build behind rpc.elysium.kinetiq.xyz? If one exists, does its pclntab name the same core/vm and uint256 v1.3.2 functions as b72783f, and do its arithmetic and jump handlers pass the cycle 30 lift scripts of theme-nitro-binary-arith-lift unchanged?
leads.why: Transfer of the cycle 30 Nitro binary lift to the one Nitro network on its own toolchain (go1.25.12) with an unnamed source. Today Elysium rests only on RPC vectors.

leads.question: Lift the AccountChange arm of State::rollback (aarch64 0x1d9826c-0x1d98354, x86_64 0x1e8d4b7-0x1e8d612) with the real hashbrown account and slot lookups. After a reverted frame that moved value or changed a nonce, does every account balance return to its pre-frame word?
leads.why: A rollback that leaves a moved balance in place inside a reverted frame would let a caller keep tokens or value without a debit. This is the half of Tempo's journal that cycle 30 left unrun.

leads.question: EIP-7773 lists 20 EIPs for Glamsterdam with no mainnet timestamp (Sepolia 1791294816). EIP-8024 is in Last Call, and the Nitro b72783f binary already holds newArbitrumAmsterdamInstructionSet. Which ArbOS version or OP Stack fork enables the Amsterdam set? In the clients that ship it (reth main, geth master, the Nitro fork), does the jump destination analysis still treat the byte after 0xe6 to 0xe8 as code, as EIP-8024 specifies?
leads.why: The critic's linear decode of research/network-risk/build/PoolManager.json finds no 0xe6, 0xe7 or 0xe8 at an instruction boundary, so the PoolManager's own 610 jump destinations cannot move. The open part is whether a client bug elsewhere in the Amsterdam set (EIP-8037 or EIP-8038 gas, EIP-7778 refunds) changes what a call returns at the gas edges that pmdiff sets 1 and 2 hit.
